newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Fighting in northern Cambodia, evacuation halted.
newsitem.headline: Fighting in northern Cambodia, evacuation halted.

text.p: Factional fighting erupted in northern Cambodia overnight, forcing cancellation of plans to evacuate tourists and aid workers from the town of Siem Reap, a Western source in the town said on Tuesday.

"There's fighting outside the city and a lot of troop movements," the source said. He said there was fighting on the road betwen Siem Reap and the Thai border, about 150 km (90 miles) to the west, and landmines had been laid on the road.

The source said the town itself was quiet on Tuesday morning but fighting had broken out overnight when forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh were withdrawing from Siem Reap to join comrades in nearby countryside.

"Last night the remaining FUNCINPEC forces were able to extricate themselves from the town after a two-day standoff," he said, referring to Ranariddh's men. Five soldiers loyal to powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen had been wounded in the fighting, the source said, citing a military official loyal to Hun Sen.
The tourists and aid workers were in a state of confusion, he said. They had hoped to travel overland to the Thai border on Tuesday.

Siem Reap town was under the control of forces loyal to Hun Sen while large areas of the surrounding countryside were under the control of forces loyal to Ranariddh. Fighting between the two camps broke out in the capital on Saturday and Hun Sen took control of Phnom Penh by Monday morning.
